blocks.text: NEW TESTAMENT
Agabus. A prophet from Judaea who foretold a great dearth, and bound his own hands and feet with Paul’s girdle.
SCRIPTURE SAYS
“A certain prophet, named Agabus” (Acts 21:10)
ERA
New Testament AD 1–60
IN THE DAYS OF
Claudius
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW THE WORD CAME
He came with other prophets “from Jerusalem unto Antioch”, stood up, and “signified by the Spirit”.
THE CALL
How the word came
He came with other prophets “from Jerusalem unto Antioch”, stood up, and “signified by the Spirit”. Acts 11:27–28
In Acts 21 “a certain prophet, named Agabus” “came down from Judæa” to Caesarea, took Paul’s girdle, bound his own hands and feet, and spoke with the words “Thus saith the Holy Ghost”. Acts 21:10–11
From the textActs tells no call and gives him no home town beyond these journeys. Acts 11:27–28 Acts 21:10

Before Claudius
ROMAN EMPEROR
Claudius
“which came to pass in the days of Claudius Cæsar.”

HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
From the textActs names him no more after Caesarea. Scripture gives no account of his death. Acts 21:10–11
TRADITION SAYS

A list of the Seventy, printed under Hippolytus' name among the “dubious and spurious pieces” in the Ante-Nicene Fathers, has “Agabus the prophet” at number 32.[9] Who says so: “On the Seventy Apostles”, ascribed to Hippolytus (printed as dubious or spurious), date not known
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
The same man
Jamieson, Fausset and Brown (1871); H. A. W. Meyer (English 1877–1879); John Gill (1746–1748)
Jamieson, Fausset and Brown: “no doubt the same as in Ac 11:28”; Meyer sees “no reason against” it; Gill reckons sixteen or seventeen years between the two scenes. Acts 11:28 Acts 21:10 [78][79][80]
Acts does not say
From the text
Acts 21:10 brings him in as “a certain prophet, named Agabus”, without referring back to Acts 11. The site’s person record joins the two. Acts 21:10
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 2
Acts 11 Acts 21
PASSAGES · 2
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Acts does not say that the Agabus of Acts 21 is the Agabus of Acts 11. This page follows the site’s person record, which joins them, as many commentators do (see the open question).
Acts does not say in so many words that the girdle word was fulfilled; it tells what happened at Jerusalem without referring back to it.
Scripture gives no family, home town or death for Agabus.
